sources.title: Bastion Square Partners II Inc. Closes Initial Public Offering and Lists on the TSX Venture Exchange as a Capital Pool Company
Bastion Square Partners II Inc. (BASQ.P) Raises $1.5 Million in IPO, Lists on TSX Venture Exchange as Capital Pool Company

brief: Bastion Square Partners II Inc., a Vancouver-based capital pool company, closed its initial public offering on November 3, 2026, raising $1.5 million in gross proceeds through the sale of 15,000,000 common shares at $0.10 each. The shares listed on the TSX Venture Exchange that day under a trading halt pending closing.

Trading in the shares, under the symbol BASQ.P, is set to resume November 9, 2026. The company now has 27,000,000 shares outstanding, of which 13,825,000 are held in escrow. Independent Trading Group (ITG), Inc. acted as agent, earning a $55,000 cash commission, a $10,000 corporate finance fee and 500,000 warrants exercisable at $0.10 until November 3, 2028.

Directors and officers were granted 2,700,000 incentive stock options at $0.10, exercisable for five years; directors also bought 1,825,000 of the offered shares themselves. The company has no business of its own: net proceeds will fund the search for an acquisition target to complete a qualifying transaction under TSX Venture Exchange rules.
body: Bastion Square Partners II Inc., a Vancouver-based capital pool company, closed its initial public offering on November 3, 2026, raising $1.5 million in gross proceeds through the sale of 15,000,000 common shares at $0.10 each. The TSX Venture Exchange approved the listing on November 2, and the shares began trading under a halt pending closing.

Trading in the shares, under the symbol BASQ.P, is scheduled to resume on November 9, 2026. Following the offering, the company has 27,000,000 common shares outstanding, of which 13,825,000 are held in escrow.

Independent Trading Group (ITG), Inc. acted as agent for the offering. It received a cash commission of $55,000, a corporate finance fee of $10,000, reimbursement of its legal fees and expenses, and 500,000 non-transferable warrants exercisable at $0.10 per share until November 3, 2028.

The company's directors and officers were granted 2,700,000 incentive stock options at an exercise price of $0.10, exercisable for five years. Directors also personally purchased 1,825,000 of the shares sold in the offering, a related-party transaction disclosed in the filing.

A capital pool company such as Bastion Square has no business or assets of its own beyond the cash raised at listing. Under TSX Venture Exchange rules, it must use the proceeds to identify and evaluate a business or asset to acquire, a process the exchange calls a qualifying transaction.

The release named Briony Bayer, the company's Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, as the contact for further information. It did not disclose any potential acquisition target or sector of interest.
